observers: Codex, during the user's explicitly authorized Android emulator test

checks.name: Muted voice and app-only projection baseline
checks.observation: Mac joined SHARE_TEST without its microphone; Android's voice dock and participant card also showed the microphone disabled. The Mac roster discovered the Android participant and its active screen publication. Android dumpsys showed TYPE_SCREEN_CAPTURE and a foreground IsolateHolderService with mediaProjection type while Clock was the top-resumed application.

checks.name: Mac remote frame and full portrait bounds
checks.observation: The Mac viewer rendered the selected Clock app as a full 576x1280 portrait image centered in the landscape stage, with the complete app bounds visible and no top/bottom crop. Two Mac screenshots about two seconds apart showed changing Clock pixels, confirming the receiver was not displaying only a frozen first frame.

checks.name: Receiver statistics consistency
checks.observation: While the Mac visibly rendered changing frames and reported the current viewer as 576x1280 at 14 FPS, its diagnostics simultaneously reported decoded 0 FPS and received 0.2 kbit/s, with receiver RTT unavailable. Voice-dock RTT was separately 4 ms. These receiver fields are inconsistent with the observed moving remote image and need source-level diagnosis; voice RTT is not receiver RTT.

checks.name: App-only hide, stop and cleanup
checks.observation: Returning Android to BOOHTACORD displayed the expected hidden-selected-app explanation. The filtered native capture log recorded visible, hidden, then projection_app_stop events. Stopping removed the Mac remote screen entry; dumpsys media_projection returned null. Both clients then left SHARE_TEST and the emulator showed an empty voice roster.

limitations: This is API 35 emulator evidence, not Pixel or other physical Android acceptance.

The Mac viewer's changing pixels prove visible receiver rendering, but sender encoded-frame counters and a trustworthy receiver decoded-frame rate were not obtained; server-side publication metrics were not queried.
This Android-to-Mac test does not establish the separate reported black-screen case for a browser-published stream after switching to the macOS client.
remaining: Trace the Mac receiver diagnostics to raw LiveKit/WebRTC stats and fix the 0-FPS/near-zero-bitrate discrepancy without changing the stream renderer; then correlate sender and receiver counters on an emulator and Pixel. Separately repeat the browser-to-Mac source-switch scenario for FE-61.
